sample_unit: LLM-generated diagnostic responses (97 DSM-5 cases x 39 demographic groups, GPT-4o analysis)

links.outcome: Change in LLM psychiatric diagnoses when patient gender and race/ethnicity cues varied with symptoms constant
links.effect: GPT-4o accuracy varied by gender (higher for female, lower for nonbinary); overall accuracy did not differ by race/ethnicity, but cultural bereavement and antisocial behavior were diagnosed exclusively in patients of color.
links.quote: Accuracy varied by gender, with higher performance for female patients and lower for nonbinary individuals.

links.outcome: Stereotyped diagnostic patterns and explanatory language across racial/ethnic groups
links.effect: Cultural bereavement and antisocial behavior were diagnosed exclusively in patients of color, and terms such as disruptive were used more frequently for Black men.
links.quote: For example, cultural bereavement and antisocial behavior-were diagnosed exclusively in patients of color, and terms such as disruptive were used more frequently for Black men.

links.outcome: LLM diagnostic accuracy across demographic subgroups
links.effect: Overall accuracy did not differ significantly by race/ethnicity, but accuracy varied by gender and biased diagnostic patterns emerged in subgroups.
links.quote: Although overall accuracy did not differ significantly by race/ethnicity, biased diagnostic patterns emerged.

screen.reason: The study conducts an audit across altered clinical vignettes to evaluate diagnostic accuracy and demographic bias (gender, race/ethnicity) of LLMs in psychiatric diagnosis, but does not test a specific deployment practice or safeguard.
